item.research_question: Can a high entropy alloy coating be deposited by laser cladding on stainless steel with improved microstructure and properties?
item.processing_route: Laser cladding with parameters: laser power 1400 W, spot diameter 3 mm, track displacement 1.2 mm, scanning speed 10 mm/s
item.test_conditions: Microstructure, composition, and properties of the coating were studied using SEM, EDS, XRD, and microhardness testing
key_findings: Significant decrease in the size of vanadium precipitates from 20-40 µm to 1-3 µm after laser cladding
Diffusion of Fe from the stainless steel into the coating material, resulting in a gradient in composition and microhardness
Microhardness of the coating decreased from 370 HV0.3 at the outer surface to 270 HV0.3 at the boundary with the substrate
Improved microstructure with no defects, pores, or cracks, and a transition zone with a thickness of about 50 µm
Entropy of mixing for the fcc solid solution in the HEA decreased after laser cladding, but remained at values ≥ 1.5R for high-entropy phases
item.mechanism: Accelerated heating, recrystallization, and rapid cooling under laser irradiation improved the microstructure of Al0.25CoCrFeNiV HEA
item.limitations: Diffusion of Fe from the matrix into the coating, which can affect the composition and properties of the coating
item.future_work: Development of parameters for laser cladding to create coatings from high entropy alloys with improved properties
quotes: the use of a relatively low laser power (1400 W) in the deposition of the Al0.25CoCrFeNiV HEAC made it possible to avoid the occurrence of a heat-affected zone in the matrix material
the presence of Fe diffusion is the main factor for obtaining a coating with a gradient in composition and microhardness
laser cladding not only improved the composition and morphology of the enriched V phase, but also increased its value entropy of mixing

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can a high entropy alloy coating be deposited by laser cladding on stainless steel with improved microstructure and properties?. System: Al0.25CoCrFeNiV high entropy alloy. Processing: Laser cladding with parameters: laser power 1400 W, spot diameter 3 mm, track displacement 1.2 mm, scanning speed 10 mm/s. Test conditions: Microstructure, composition, and properties of the coating were studied using SEM, EDS, XRD, and microhardness testing. Findings: Significant decrease in the size of vanadium precipitates from 20-40 µm to 1-3 µm after laser cladding; Diffusion of Fe from the stainless steel into the coating material, resulting in a gradient in composition and microhardness; Microhardness of the coating decreased from 370 HV0.3 at the outer surface to 270 HV0.3 at the boundary with the substrate; Improved microstructure with no defects, pores, or cracks, and a transition zone with a thickness of about 50 µm; Entropy of mixing for the fcc solid solution in the HEA decreased after laser cladding, but remained at values ≥ 1.5R for high-entropy phases. Mechanism: Accelerated heating, recrystallization, and rapid cooling under laser irradiation improved the microstructure of Al0.25CoCrFeNiV HEA. Limitations: Diffusion of Fe from the matrix into the coating, which can affect the composition and properties of the coating. Future work: Development of parameters for laser cladding to create coatings from high entropy alloys with improved properties. Quote: "the use of a relatively low laser power (1400 W) in the deposition of the Al0.25CoCrFeNiV HEAC made it possible to avoid the occurrence of a heat-affected zone in the matrix material"
